_comment: Which books are paid, and what has to be bought to read them.
This file is the single source of truth. index_json.py stamps each row of
data/index.json with its tier so the client can draw a lock without asking
the server; split_content.py uses it to decide which book files leave the
public deploy; api/main.py re-reads it and is the only opinion that counts.
A book missing from `books` is free. A value is an sku, matched against the
entitlements table; the sku 'all' unlocks everything and needs no entry.
Moving a book between tiers is an edit here plus a rerun of the two tools —
nobody's purchased rows have to change, because rows carry skus, not books.
_pending: Empty on purpose, for now. Marking a book paid moves its JSON out of
site/data/ — and until api.config.js carries a working API base, the app
would ask for a file that is no longer there and show 'could not load'
rather than a lock. The API base cannot be filled in before Railway has
built once and issued a domain, and Railway cannot build before this is
pushed. So the first deploy ships with nothing gated.
Turning it on later is this map plus a rerun of split_content.py and
